compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two colleagues in a planning meeting who both ask which assumptions are worth testing. That similarity would fit either description. The question alone gives you little to go on about E/I.

Shared N and T help explain why both profiles emphasize possibilities and consistent reasoning. In type dynamics, shared P means both show Ne, a perceiving process, in their outward engagement. Those are features of the model. Both people could generate useful ideas or test a premise carefully.

For ENTP, outward-facing Ne is dominant and inward-facing Ti supports it. For INTP, Ti is dominant and Ne supports it. They can look similar from the outside because both use Ne as their outward-facing process. In the model, the difference is which process leads overall. A meeting cannot tell you which function leads for an individual.

### ### ENTP and INTP: two ways to plan the same product trial

In a fictional store trial, the team has one new flavour, the same shelf space and three days. One line of thought opens up options for shelf placement and timing. Another defines what the team would count as success, such as a difference in sales under comparable conditions. Either ENTP or INTP could make both contributions.

Exploring alternatives and checking the logic of the trial draw on processes shared by both types in the model. Look across several situations before drawing any inference about preference. The same person might talk through one problem with colleagues and prefer time alone for another. A role that requires brainstorming in public or preparing a private analysis gives you little evidence about what that person would choose freely.

compare_blocks.body:
In this fictional trial, both people have the same product, instructions, data, deadlines and decision-making authority. Each has access to colleagues and time to think privately.

| Shared situation | ENTP: possible outward focus | INTP: possible inward focus | What the row illustrates |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two colleagues in a planning meeting who both ask which assumptions are worth testing. That similarity would fit either description. The question alone gives you little to go on about E/I.

Shared N and T help explain why both profiles emphasize possibilities and consistent reasoning. In type dynamics, shared P means both show Ne, a perceiving process, in their outward engagement. Those are features of the model. Both people could generate useful ideas or test a premise carefully.

For ENTP, outward-facing Ne is dominant and inward-facing Ti supports it. For INTP, Ti is dominant and Ne supports it. They can look similar from the outside because both use Ne as their outward-facing process. In the model, the difference is which process leads overall. A meeting cannot tell you which function leads for an individual.

### ### ENTP and INTP: two ways to plan the same product trial

In a fictional store trial, the team has one new flavour, the same shelf space and three days. One line of thought opens up options for shelf placement and timing. Another defines what the team would count as success, such as a difference in sales under comparable conditions. Either ENTP or INTP could make both contributions.

These fictional scenes illustrate how people might weigh different considerations. Either type can take either approach. Assign responsibility based on the work and who can do it.

### ### ENTP and INTP: the store finds a price tag error

In a fictional store trial, several shelf labels show a lower price than the checkout system. Both people have the same transaction records and neither can set store policy. They can report the mismatch to the person responsible, who can address the price discrepancy under the store’s procedures.

The analysis team can then log the affected interval and decide whether those sales can fairly be compared with the planned trial. The discrepancy illustrates why a sales figure needs context. It was an unintended change, so the team cannot treat the result as evidence from a controlled price test. Either type could flag the mismatch or question the comparison.

### ### ENTP and INTP: classifying an unusual support ticket

In a fictional support case, a customer reports a squeaking shoe, but the team cannot reproduce it on inspection. Both colleagues can work from the same report and ask follow-up questions. It helps to ask when the sound occurs and record the surface and frequency in fields the next person can use.

Open-ended questions can surface a detail the form missed. Consistent fields make it easier to compare similar complaints and hand the case over. Either type can combine the two. Choose how much detail to collect based on what the case needs and what the next person can verify.

### ### ENTP and INTP: sales are below forecast

In a fictional trial, fifth-day sales are 30% below forecast. Both colleagues can review the same sales and stock records and suggest changes. They might question whether the forecast allowed for a competitor’s promotion, or consider testing whether shelf placement matters.

Checking assumptions can reveal that the comparison was flawed. A well-defined change can generate new evidence, but several simultaneous changes make the outcome harder to interpret. With two days left, the team can agree which question it has enough time and data to answer. Either type can examine the forecast and propose a test.

The example illustrates how clarifying terms and exploring alternatives can complement each other. The renter can write down unclear terms and proposed changes, and ask a qualified local adviser about the agreement if needed. Neither approach identifies an ENTP or INTP.

sections.body_md:
Imagine two colleagues in a planning meeting who both ask which assumptions are worth testing. That similarity would fit either description. The question alone gives you little to go on about E/I.

Shared N and T help explain why both profiles emphasize possibilities and consistent reasoning. In type dynamics, shared P means both show Ne, a perceiving process, in their outward engagement. Those are features of the model. Both people could generate useful ideas or test a premise carefully.

For ENTP, outward-facing Ne is dominant and inward-facing Ti supports it. For INTP, Ti is dominant and Ne supports it. They can look similar from the outside because both use Ne as their outward-facing process. In the model, the difference is which process leads overall. A meeting cannot tell you which function leads for an individual.

### ### ENTP and INTP: two ways to plan the same product trial

In a fictional store trial, the team has one new flavour, the same shelf space and three days. One line of thought opens up options for shelf placement and timing. Another defines what the team would count as success, such as a difference in sales under comparable conditions. Either ENTP or INTP could make both contributions.

Exploring alternatives and checking the logic of the trial draw on processes shared by both types in the model. For the E/I comparison, hold the question constant and consider where attention goes when the person has a choice: toward the shelves and discussion in front of them, or toward working through their impressions and ideas privately.

Too many changes at once can make it hard to tell what affected sales. A rigid success criterion can also rule out a useful idea before anyone considers it. The deadline, staffing and amount of usable data should guide that trade-off.

Look across several situations before drawing any inference about preference. The same person might talk through one problem with colleagues and prefer time alone for another. A role that requires brainstorming in public or preparing a private analysis gives you little evidence about what that person would choose freely.
